card.title: A Kinder Version
card.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery thinks your portrait would suit a more adventurous exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're showing a fridge full of teeth. What did they say about mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That the face doesn't immediately reveal what you intended.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's you. They called it unrecognisable, didn't they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They think knowing the sitter would help. I'll attend your next opening with a matching shirt.

mechanism: A softens an artist's rejection by translating harsh feedback into gentler interpretation and a supportive practical gesture.
confusable: Unlike covering A's own responsibility, A must aim the edited truth at protecting B from hurt.
comparison: A portrait sitter offers to make recognition easier; the other alternative replaces a harsh birthday exclusion with companionship.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
